newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sells balance stake in two estate firms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sells balance stake in two estate firms.

text.p: The Sri Lanka government is selling its remaining shares in previously privatised Kegalle Plantations and Kelani Valley Plantations, a stock exchange official said on Wednesday.
"Parcels of 3.8 million shares in Kegalle Plantations and 1.5 million in Kelani Valley, have been introduced for sale at 31.50 rupees and 31, respectively," he said.
The 10-rupee Kegalle share was trading at 35.50 rupees on Wednesday, while Kelani Valley was quoted at 31.50.
The two parcels will be kept on overnight bid for three days in line with stock exchange rules governing trading of five percent or more of a company's issued capital.
The government started reducing its shareholding in the six privatised estate firms on Tuesday by selling 3.8 million shares of Agalawatte Plantations for 35.50 rupees.
The government decided in March to cut its holding in the six privatised estate firms to one 'golden share', which enables it to intervene in the company in the event of malpractices.

It privatised Kegalle Plantations, Kelani Valley Plantations, Bogawantalawa Plantations, Agalawatte Plantations, Horana Plantations and Kotagala Plantations in 1995 by selling 51 percent of each firm's issued capital of 20 million shares to a strategic investor and 20 percent to the public.
Ten percent was reserved for estate workers while the government retained 19 percent or 3.8 million shares in each firm.
Sri Lanka began restructuring the 23 plantation firms which own some 600,000 hectares of tea, rubber and coconut in 1992 by privatising management, which later spread to ownership.
